html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold with Copy and Add, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and while you run the level ticks three results — the level completes, every bottle in the right bin, under par.

Ten bottles — small, medium and large, in three colours, some of them broken — come out of the hopper one per release. Sort them by height into four bins: broken bottles to bin 1, small to 2, medium to 3, large to 4. The filler is there but not scored on this level; leave it alone. Par is 150 s.

The plan is the simplest one that works: release a bottle, let it run past the gantry, remember what the gantry saw, fire the right pusher when the bottle reaches it, wait for it to land, release the next. One bottle on the belt at a time means one set of memory bits, and that is the whole idea of this level: a sensor tells you something for a fraction of a second, and the program has to keep it until it is needed further down the belt.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

The run circuit

Rung 0 is chapter 4’s seal-in. On this machine Stop is a plain normally-open button, so it is XIO(Stop_PB), not the XIC(Stop) of the bottle line, whose stop button is normally closed — read the device’s settings, not your habits. E_Stop is 1 while the E-stop is healthy. Rung 1 runs the belt and lights the run lamp whenever the line runs; on this level the belt never stops.

Releasing one bottle

The release rung fires once — the one-shot — when the line runs, no bottle is in progress (XIO(Busy)) and the hopper’s exit is clear. On the same scan it latches Busy, so nothing else is released until this bottle is dealt with, and unlatches the four memory bits, so this bottle starts with a clean slate. The hopper is in edge mode: one rising edge of Infeed_Release, one bottle.

A way out of Busy: the watchdog

Busy is latched, so the next thing to write is a way to free it. Rungs 3–4 are the watchdog: while a bottle is in progress a 16 s timer runs, and when it is done the line is freed anyway — a bottle nobody wanted, or a bug, runs to the end of the belt and the next one is released. Written straight after the latch, it also keeps the line feeding while you write the rest: every bottle runs to the end and 16 s later the next one drops, so each rung below can be tested in Run the moment it is written. A latch with no way out written next to it is how lines stall.

Remembering what the gantry saw

Four latches. Each beam is broken only while the bottle passes it — about half a second — but the pushers are metres downstream, so the program latches what it saw. A small bottle sets only Is_Low; a medium sets Is_Low and Is_Mid; a large sets all three; the crack eye sets Is_Broken. Nothing clears them except the next release.

Firing the right pusher

Each pusher has its own eye just ahead of the arm; the rung pushes while that eye sees the bottle and the memory says the bottle belongs in this bin. The size tests are written as this beam and not the next one up: small is low-not-mid, medium is mid-not-high, large is high. Every whole-bottle bin tests XIO(Is_Broken) first: a broken bottle is broken whatever its size, and bin 1 is upstream, so it has already gone by the time a broken bottle could reach bin 2 — but the test costs nothing and saves you when the bins are reordered.

Freeing the line

Rung 13 latches Done when any pusher fires, because the pusher’s eye — and so the pusher rung — goes false the moment the bottle is pushed off the belt. A timer fed straight from Div2 would see half a second, never 1.5. Rungs 14-15 give the bottle a second and a half to land, then free the line and reset the watchdog: that bottle was dealt with, so the next one gets its own 16 s. The RES(Trip) matters because of where the watchdog sits. Its timer is above the release, and Busy is freed at the bottom of one scan and latched again by the release near the top of the next, so the timer never sees Busy off and never resets by itself; without the RES it would time across bottles and free the line early.

Watch for: the res

The first draft of this program had XIC(After.DN)OTU(Busy); with no RES, and released bottles in pairs. Walk the scan: the timer finishes and rung 15 unlatches Busy. Next scan, rung 2 sees Busy off, releases a bottle and latches Busy again — so rung 14’s timer sees its rung true, as it was last scan. It never saw the rung go false, so it never reset: it is still done, and rung 15 unlatches Busy again, and the next bottle is released right behind the first. A timer resets only when its rung is false for a whole scan. When the thing that ends a cycle also starts the next one, reset the timer yourself.

Run it

Run mode, press Start on the console. A bottle drops, runs past the gantry (watch the four Is_ bits in Monitor Tags latch), reaches its pusher and goes into its bin; a moment later the next one drops. The header counts Correct and Wrong; the Simulator Log names every bottle and the bin it landed in. A run of this program on 10 of 10 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 100 s against a par of 150 s: 1200 points and three stars.

Try It

Take XIO(Is_Broken) out of the small-bin rung and set the hopper’s Broken bottles to 60 % — then move bin 1 to the far end of the line (swap the pushers’ names). A broken small bottle now reaches bin 2 first. Put the test back. Then shorten After to 300 ms and see what the next bottle does to a bottle still sliding into its bin.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: Start seals Run in through its own contact; Stop (a plain button here) or a tripped E-stop breaks the seal

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt and the run lamp follow Run
rungs.words: When Run is on, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle when the line is free, mark it busy, and forget what we knew about the last bottle
rungs.words: When Run is on, Busy is off, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false), latches Busy on, unlatches Is_Low, unlatches Is_Mid, unlatches Is_High and unlatches Is_Broken.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  3. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  4. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Busy) Output Latch does: latches Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Is_Low) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Low. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Is_Mid) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Mid. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Is_High) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_High. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Is_Broken) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Broken. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: WATCHDOG, right after the release that latched Busy: if no pusher frees the line, the bottle has run the whole belt
rungs.words: When Busy is on, the rung runs the timer Trip toward 16000 ms (16 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Busy) Examine If Closed asks: true when Busy is on.
  2. TON(Trip,16000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Trip toward 16000 ms (16 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Trip counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: free the line anyway, so the line keeps feeding while you write the rest

pred.q: Trip.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Busy is left as it was and Trip is left alone. It stops at XIC(Trip.DN).

rungs.words: When Trip.DN (the done bit of Trip) is on, the rung unlatches Busy and resets Trip.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trip.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trip.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. RES(Trip) Reset does: resets Trip. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Busy when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: GANTRY: the low beam is broken by every size
rungs.words: When PE_Low (Height beam at 30 px: blocked by every size) is on, the rung latches Is_Low on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Low is on.
  2. OTL(Is_Low) Output Latch does: latches Is_Low on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Is_Low stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: the middle beam by medium and large

pred.q: PE_Mid is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Is_Mid latches on.

rungs.words: When PE_Mid (Height beam at 44 px: blocked by M and L) is on, the rung latches Is_Mid on.
rungs.ltr:

  2. OTL(Is_Mid) Output Latch does: latches Is_Mid on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: the high beam by large only
rungs.words: When PE_High (Height beam at 52 px: blocked by L only) is on, the rung latches Is_High on.
rungs.ltr:

pats.why: Is_High stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: the crack eye sees broken bottles

pred.q: Crack_Sensor is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Is_Broken is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Crack_Sensor).

rungs.words: When Crack_Sensor (Crack eye: the bottle in front of it is broken) is on, the rung latches Is_Broken on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Crack_Sensor) Examine If Closed asks: true when Crack_Sensor is on.
  2. OTL(Is_Broken) Output Latch does: latches Is_Broken on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Is_Broken stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: BIN 1, broken: push while the bottle is at the pusher’s eye
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on and Is_Broken is on, the rung turns Div1 (Diverter 1 cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. XIC(Is_Broken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_Broken is on.
  3. OTE(Div1) Output Energize does: turns Div1 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: BIN 2, small: low beam but not the middle one

pred.q: PE_Div2 is on, Is_Broken is off, Is_Low is off and Is_Mid is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Div2 is off. It stops at XIC(Is_Low).

rungs.words: When PE_Div2 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 2) is on, Is_Broken is off, Is_Low is on and Is_Mid is off, the rung turns Div2 (Diverter 2 cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div2) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div2 is on.
  2. XIO(Is_Broken) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Broken is off.
  3. XIC(Is_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_Low is on.
  4. XIO(Is_Mid) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Mid is off.
  5. OTE(Div2) Output Energize does: turns Div2 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: BIN 3, medium: middle beam but not the high one
rungs.words: When PE_Div3 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 3) is on, Is_Broken is off, Is_Mid is on and Is_High is off, the rung turns Div3 (Diverter 3 cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div3) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div3 is on.
  2. XIO(Is_Broken) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Broken is off.
  3. XIC(Is_Mid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_Mid is on.
  4. XIO(Is_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_High is off.
  5. OTE(Div3) Output Energize does: turns Div3 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 12

pred.q: PE_Div4 is on, Is_Broken is on and Is_High is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Div4 is off. It stops at XIO(Is_Broken).

rungs.words: When PE_Div4 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 4) is on, Is_Broken is off and Is_High is on, the rung turns Div4 (Diverter 4 cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div4) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div4 is on.
  2. XIO(Is_Broken) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Broken is off.
  3. XIC(Is_High) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_High is on.
  4. OTE(Div4) Output Energize does: turns Div4 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: A pusher fired: remember it, because the eye clears the moment the bottle is pushed
rungs.words: When either (Div1 (Diverter 1 cylinder) is on), (Div2 (Diverter 2 cylinder) is on), (Div3 (Diverter 3 cylinder) is on) or (Div4 (Diverter 4 cylinder) is on), the rung latches Done on.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when Div1 is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Div2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Div2 is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Div3) Examine If Closed asks: true when Div3 is on.
    Path 4
    1. XIC(Div4) Examine If Closed asks: true when Div4 is on.
  2. OTL(Done) Output Latch does: latches Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: Give the bottle a second and a half to land

pred.q: Done is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: After times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Done is on, the rung runs the timer After toward 1500 ms (1.5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Done is on.
  2. TON(After,1500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer After toward 1500 ms (1.5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: After counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: Free the line for the next bottle and reset the watchdog; RES(After), or the timer stays done through the next release
rungs.words: When After.DN (the done bit of After) is on, the rung unlatches Busy, unlatches Done, resets After and resets Trip.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(After.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when After.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. RES(After) Reset does: resets After. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 4
    1. RES(Trip) Reset does: resets Trip. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Busy when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.
